summary: A file-based API client for one developer: requests as YAML in git, environments with secrets from the shell, a runner with assertions that exits non-zero for CI, chaining a token from one call into the next, history with diffs, and an importer for Postman collections. Bruno is the open-source answer; this is the 500-line version you own.

stack.why: no GUI, no cloud, no sync problem

stack.choice: YAML files in git plus a SQLite history

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: Try Bruno first
prerequisites.why: If it fits, use it and stop; it is free and file-based. This build is for wanting a version you can read in an afternoon.

prerequisites.name: A Postman collection export and an API to hit
prerequisites.why: Phase 5 imports it; every phase needs a real API to test against.
prerequisites.get: Postman > Collection > Export (v2.1). Any public API or your own local server for tests.

prerequisites.name: Where secrets live: the shell, never files
prerequisites.why: Requests reference {{env.NAME}}; values come from environment variables.
prerequisites.get: Export them in your shell profile or a .env you never commit.

env.name: API_TOKEN
env.where: An example secret a request references as {{env.API_TOKEN}}.

phases.title: Run one request
phases.goal: YAML in, pretty response out, secrets only from the shell.

steps.do: Create the CLI project and the request and environment file formats
steps.detail: requests/<name>.yaml: method, url, headers, query, body, auth, asserts. environments/<name>.yaml: key-value pairs referenced as {{name}}.
commands: mkdir api-cli && cd api-cli && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module && npm install yaml@2

steps.do: Implement api run <file> --env <name> with variable substitution and {{env.NAME}} from process.env

check: A GET and a JSON POST print status, headers, pretty JSON and latency
A missing variable fails naming itself

phases.title: Assertions
phases.goal: Status and JSON-path asserts with a non-zero exit.

steps.do: Implement asserts on status and JSON paths
Exit 1 with a readable diff on failure

check: A wrong status exits 1 with a diff

phases.title: Collections and chaining
phases.goal: Run a folder in order; capture values between requests.

steps.do: api run <folder> in filename order with pass counts
capture: a JSON path into a variable for later requests

check: A login feeds its token to the next request
The folder run reports pass counts

phases.title: History and diff
phases.goal: Every run recorded; diff the last two responses.

steps.do: Record runs in SQLite: request, environment, status, latency, size, body hash

phases.title: Import

steps.do: Parse Postman v2.1 JSON into requests and environments

check: An exported collection runs after import

phases.title: Share with a team
phases.goal: Only if others use it: publish the CLI and enforce it in CI.

steps.do: Publish to a private npm registry or as a git dependency
Run the collection in CI on every deploy with secrets from the CI store

check: A teammate installs and runs the collection
CI fails when an assertion fails

product.outcome: API tests that live with the code, run in CI, and never leak a secret through a synced workspace.

operations.incident: A leaked secret is rotated at its source; files never held it.

releaseGate: Secrets verified absent from every file
CI run passes on a real collection

notIncluded: Team sync, mock servers, monitors, the visual editor: the seat price.
after: A local web UI over the same files
